terms.grammar: verb, third conjugation: what is surrounded in the accusative; in the passive, what surrounds it in the ablative
evidence: Caes. BG 1.38: flūmen Dūbis … paene tōtum oppidum cingit (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Fl. 27: prōvincia marī cīncta (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Of what lies or stands all round a thing: a river, walls, the sea, a crowd. Its other everyday sense is “gird” (a sword, a belt), and so “wreathe, crown” (Lewis & Short).

terms.grammar: verb, first conjugation: aliquid alicui, put one thing round another, or aliquid aliquā rē, surround a thing with another
evidence: Tac. Germ. 16.2: suam quisque domum spatiō circumdat
terms.comment: Of what someone puts round a thing: a wall, a fence, a trench, guards, or one’s arms round a neck (bracchia collō, Ov. M. 9.459, Lewis & Short).

phrases.english: each man surrounds his house with open ground

phrases.latin: vīdī vīllam extrūctam lapide quadrātō, mūrum circumdatum silvae
phrases.english: I saw a house built of squared stone, and a wall put round the wood

phrases.latin: prīmāsque in lītore sēdēs castrōrum in mōrem pinnīs atque aggere cingit
phrases.english: and he rings the first dwellings on the shore with battlements and a rampart, like a camp

sources: Lewis & Short: cingo · Lewis & Short: circumdo
